lessons.titleEnglish: Read the Manufacturer Sheet Before the Flashing Goes On
lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Read a manufacturer instruction sheet, find the key specs, and explain the steps to the crew
lessons.focusEnglishSource: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: You are the crew lead and the AI is a crew member ready to install flashing from habit: read the key steps of the manufacturer sheet aloud, explain what has to happen before and after each step, and get agreement to follow the sheet.

words.en: Before installing, you have to read the sheet.
What does the sheet say about the overlap?
That's what the manufacturer asks for.
Hey, have you already read it?
Could you give me a moment, please?

grammarExamplesEnglish: Before installing the flashing, you have to read the sheet.
After reading each step, we have to check the material.
readingEnglish: Before putting the step flashing on the sidewall, Rogelio takes the spec sheet out of the box.
Rogelio: Before installing, you have to read the sheet, even if we've been doing this for years.
Rogelio: The sheet rules, not habit.
Rogelio reads step 1 of the manufacturer instructions out loud.
Step 1: Before placing the flashing, install the underlayment over the deck and run it up the sidewall according to the specification.
Step 2: Place one piece of step flashing on each course, with the minimum overlap this sheet indicates.
Step 3: Fasten each piece only to the deck, never to the wall, with the specified fastener.
Step 4: After placing the flashing, the siding must cover it; do not use sealant instead of flashing.
Warning: If you do not follow these steps, the product may fail and the manufacturer may not cover the damage.
Kevin: Hey, have you already read all of it?
Rogelio: Yes, and you have to read it too; don't do it from memory.
Rogelio: After reading each step, you have to check whether the material on the truck is the same as on the sheet.
Rogelio: What does the sheet say about the overlap?
Kevin: It says you have to use the sheet's minimum overlap, and that the chimney and the pipe boot have another section.
Then the homeowner asks when they're starting, and Rogelio answers: Could you give me a moment, please?
Rogelio: That's what the manufacturer asks for, and that's how we do it.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Rogelio reads step 1 of the manufacturer instructions out loud.
Before installing, you have to read the sheet.
Rogelio places one piece of step flashing on each course.
Fasten each piece only to the deck.
If you do not follow these steps, the product may fail.

lessons.titleEnglish: Unexpected Rotten Deck: Change Order with the Homeowner
lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Tell a homeowner what you found under the old roof, propose the repair, and get a signed change order
lessons.focusEnglishSource: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: You are the crew lead and the AI is the homeowner: describe what you found during the tear-off and what it looked like, propose the repair with its cost and extra time using the conditional, and ask for a signature on the change order.

words.en: When we removed the shingles, we found rotten wood.
The deck was soft in this section.
I would recommend replacing three sheets.
It would cost more and take an extra day.
Shall I show you the photos?
I need your signature on the change order.

grammarExamplesEnglish: When we removed the shingles, we found rotten wood.
The deck was soft; replacing it would cost more.
readingEnglish: At nine in the morning, the crew finished the tear-off on the north side.
Kevin was stepping carefully when he felt the deck sinking.
Kevin: Hey, come look at this.
Rogelio checked the area with the pry bar: the wood was black and damp, and a rafter had stains.
Rogelio took photos of the damage and marked the edge with paint.
Then he went down to talk with the homeowner, Mr. Ramírez.
Rogelio: Mr. Ramírez, when we removed the shingles, we found rotten wood.
Rogelio: The deck was soft in this section, near the chimney, and it looked like water had been getting in for years.
Rogelio: Shall I show you the photos?
Mr. Ramírez: Yes, please. And that wasn't in the estimate?
Rogelio: No, because nobody could see it before the tear-off; that's what the change order is for.
Rogelio: I would recommend replacing three sheets of plywood and checking the rafter.
Rogelio: It would cost more and take an extra day, and the extra cost appears here, in writing, as the contract says.
Rogelio: We can't cover rotten wood, because the new nails wouldn't hold well.
Mr. Ramírez: All right, then do it.
Rogelio: Thank you; I need your signature on the change order, because without your authorization we can't start the repair.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Rogelio finds rotten wood near the chimney.
When we removed the shingles, we found rotten wood.
The deck was soft in this section.
It would cost more and take an extra day.
I would recommend replacing three sheets of plywood.

lessons.objectiveEnglishSource: Handle a short delivery: get dates from the supplier, compare a substitute, and give the new plan
lessons.speakingEnglishSource: You are the crew lead and the AI is the supplier: find out what is missing and when it will arrive, compare the substitute with the original product, and say what you will do next using the future and ir a.

words.en: We're going to use another brand.
It's just as durable, but heavier.
This color is closer to the original.
I'm going to send you the photo of the color.
Can you give me a hand?

grammarExamplesEnglish: The rest will arrive Thursday; today we're going to finish the underlayment.
This shingle is heavier than the other one, but just as durable.
readingEnglish: At seven, the supplier called Rogelio with bad news.
Supplier: I'm sorry, the order won't arrive complete, because we don't have that color in stock.
Rogelio: When will the rest arrive?
Supplier: The factory says it will arrive at the warehouse on Thursday, but it's not certain.
Rogelio: That would be a four-day delay, and the customer wants to finish sooner.
Supplier: I have the same architectural shingle from another brand, at the same price.
Supplier: It's just as durable, but heavier, and the color is very similar.
Rogelio: The architectural one from another brand works for me, but I'm not going to accept three-tab shingle; the contract says architectural.
Rogelio: Send me the spec sheet, and before deciding I'm going to talk to the customer.
Then Rogelio called Mrs. Díaz, the homeowner.
Rogelio: Ma'am, the supplier has a substitute, and this color is closer to the original than the others.
Rogelio: I'm going to send you the photo of the color, and if you approve it, the delivery will be early tomorrow.
Mrs. Díaz approved the change by text, and Rogelio asked for a new invoice.
Then he gathered the crew next to the truck.
Rogelio: We're going to use another brand, and tomorrow two pallets will arrive.
Rogelio: Today we're going to finish the underlayment and the drip edge, and tomorrow we'll start on the shingles.
Rogelio: Kevin, can you give me a hand with these rolls?

verbs.exampleEnglish: I'm going to send you the photo of the color.
We're going to use another brand.
If you approve it, the delivery will be early tomorrow.
Today we're going to finish the underlayment and the drip edge.
